messages:
anna-sec: Heads-up — SOC just forwarded a customer report saying their audit events show an action by user:service-account:relic-processor at 2026-03-15T18:12:03Z but our RBAC change shows that service-account was removed on 2026-03-15T17:55:00Z. Need timeline reconciliation.
javier-sre: On it. Can you paste the customer event (redacted) and the RBAC change PR/commit id?
anna-sec: Customer snippet (redacted): 
```json
{"timestamp":"2026-03-15T18:12:03Z","actor":"service-account:relic-processor","action":"kms.decrypt","resource":"/projects/prod-keyring/cryptoKeys/primary","audit_id":"evt-9a3f2"}
```
RBAC change: PR #824, commit b1c3f7, merged 2026-03-15T17:54:49Z by meera-eng.
meera-eng: I merged a fix that removed the service-account binding from role/relic-processor at 17:54:49Z. The merge triggered a terraform apply that finished at 17:56:12Z according to deploy-bot.
deploy-bot: terraform apply completed: plan_id=pl-42, apply_start=2026-03-15T17:55:30Z, apply_end=2026-03-15T17:56:12Z, triggered_by=meera-eng
javier-sre: So customer saw event at 18:12:03Z — ~16 minutes after the apply. Could be a replay, or KMS key policy still allowed decrypt via key IAM, or there are cached credentials. Need KMS audit trace and auth logs.
audit-bot: audit-log: query results for audit_id=evt-9a3f2 -> origin_ip=34.128.12.9, bearer=oauth-token, auth_method=service-account-key, receipt_ts=2026-03-15T18:12:02.987Z, kms_audit_entry=true
meera-eng: I'm pulling internal auth logs for that service-account. One moment.
meera-eng: Internal auth ledger shows token issued to service-account:relic-processor at 2026-03-15T16:50:10Z (long-lived), last refreshed 2026-03-15T17:20:00Z. No revocation event in our token service at merge time.
tom-privacy: If the token was long-lived it could still be valid even after removing IAM binding — removing binding stops future minting but doesn't revoke already issued tokens. Do we have token revocation in the RBAC change plan?
anna-sec: PR #824 did not include a revocation step. That's an oversight.
javier-sre: Action: confirm whether KMS accepted the request because it relied on the presentation of a valid OAuth token vs IAM binding evaluation at time of request. We need KMS request logs and KMS policy eval for that request.
meera-eng: Querying KMS logs... found decrypt request matching audit_id evt-9a3f2. KMS log: 
```json
{"request_id":"r-77b","request_ts":"2026-03-15T18:12:02Z","principal":"service-account:relic-processor","principal_claims":{"sub":"svc-relic-001","token_iat":"2026-03-15T16:50:10Z"},"policy_evaluation":"ALLOW","key_variant":"primary-v2"}
```
Policy evaluation used binding membership cached by IAM cache tier (cache TTL 900s) — cache last refresh was 2026-03-15T17:55:20Z.
javier-sre: TTL 900s = 15 minutes. Merge completed 17:54:49, apply ended 17:56:12, cache last refresh 17:55:20. That explains it: the IAM policy cache still had the old binding until ~18:10:20Z. The request at 18:12:02Z was after TTL but close — why ALLOW? Maybe the cache was refreshed but KMS consulted an alternate cache or we had a clock skew.
meera-eng: Checking cache refresh logs and host times now.
meera-eng: Host clock on the IAM cache node iam-cache-3 shows NTP offset +32s at 17:55:20; subsequent refresh at 18:10:20 failed with 503 to IAM-controlplane. Fallback used stale copy. So KMS policy evaluation used stale binding.
tom-privacy: So root cause: we removed binding but didn't revoke tokens and cache TTL + outage allowed a stale allow to persist. Customer-facing message should explain that their audit shows a decrypt by that principal; we must confirm whether data access occurred and whether to rotate keys.
anna-sec: Confirmed: decrypt returned status OK for that request; we need to surface that to customer and propose mitigations (key rotation, token revocation, change cache TTL). Also need to add a step in RBAC playbook to include revocation for long-lived tokens.
javier-sre: Quick remediation steps: 1) Revoke active tokens for service-account relic-processor (iamctl revoke-tokens svc-relic-001), 2) rotate primary key and schedule re-encrypt if necessary, 3) reduce IAM cache TTL and add monitoring for failed refreshes.
meera-eng: I've created follow-up PR to change terraform to include a revocation hook: PR #829, and a config change to reduce cache TTL from 900 to 60 seconds in iam-cache config. Also added an alert on cache-refresh 5xx -> pager.
anna-sec: For customer-facing audit validation: propose we provide the full audit_event JSON (with IP and request_id) and an explanation: timeline, cause (cache + no revocation), remediation taken. Ask customer if they want key rotation. Draft below.
meera-eng: Draft message: "We confirmed a KMS decrypt at 2026-03-15T18:12:02Z by service-account:relic-processor. This occurred due to an IAM cache TTL and a transient refresh failure; the RBAC removal was merged at 17:54:49Z but tokens had not been revoked. We have revoked tokens and rotated the key. We can provide the raw audit event and a timeline on request." Thoughts?
tom-privacy: Language looks good. Add explicit statement about no evidence of lateral movement or additional privilege escalations; include offer for key rotation and extended audit logs export.
javier-sre: Agreed. I'll attach the audit_event JSON and a signed timeline (signed by security) and send to SOC for customer delivery.
anna-sec: One more follow-up: add automated check in our RBAC playbook that when removing a binding with principals that can have long-lived tokens, the PR must include either a token revocation step or admin confirmation. I'll own the doc update.
meera-eng: I'll push PR #829 now and coordinate with infra to deploy cache TTL change.
deploy-bot: enqueue deploy: config=iam-cache, change_id=cfg-112, scheduled=2026-03-16T02:00:00Z UTC
anna-sec: Thanks everyone. Marking this thread resolved for reconstruction; will file post-incident note and customer note drafts.
javier-sre: :lock: :white_check_mark:
meera-eng: :wave:
